sections.h2: What should I know before selling a house in Edison, NJ?
sections.html:
Edison is a Middlesex County township of about 30 square miles where the sale usually hinges on one local document, the Residential Resale Certificate, plus a state smoke certificate that has to come first. Nothing about those steps is hard, but each has lead time, so start them as soon as a buyer signs a contract.

The Census Bureau counts 109,077 residents for 2025 and 38,098 households. Roughly 61 percent of homes are owner occupied, and owners report a median home value of $496,900 for 2020 to 2024. Median household income is $125,145, and 47.7 percent of residents were born abroad.

sections.h2: How did Edison get its name, and why does it matter to a seller?
sections.html:
The township carries the inventor's name because voters changed it in 1954, and it sits on the ground where Thomas Edison ran his Menlo Park laboratory from 1876. The place was earlier called Raritan Township and was carved out of Piscataway and Woodbridge. Colonial-era buildings still stand near Piscatawaytown in South Edison, and three are listed nationally: the Laing House, the Benjamin Shotwell House and the Homestead Farm at Oak Ridge.

The township has many named sections, among them Stelton, Menlo Park, Oak Tree, Raritan Manor, Clara Barton, Lindenau and Washington Park. A house that has changed hands more than once is more likely to carry a finished basement, deck or addition from an earlier owner, and those are the items the township inspector checks for permits.

sections.h2: What does the Edison resale certificate require?
sections.html:
Edison Township Ordinance 14-1.6 says a Certificate for Change of Ownership must be obtained before the property closes, and the township form warns of fines up to $2,000 for skipping it. The application fee is $150, paid by certified check, credit card or money order. The form says no cash, no personal checks and no refunds. Code Enforcement takes the application by email at the resale address printed on the form and then calls for a card payment.

Timing is the part that trips people up. One line of the form asks for the inspection at least four weeks before the closing date, and another says three weeks, so plan on four. A smoke certificate must already exist before the resale certificate can be issued, and the inspector wants a copy on site.

What the Edison inspector checks on a one or two family home
AreaWhat the form asks for
PermitsAdditions, finished basements or attics, garage conversions, patios, decks, pools and spas need verified permits
Pools and spasFence and childproof gate
Stairs and railsSecure guardrails and handrails; stair riser openings under 4 inches
MechanicalsWater heater with relief valve and piping ending 6 inches off the floor; tight flue connections; shut-off valves on gas appliances
DryerVented outside, not into a garage, attic or basement
OutsideHouse numbers at least 4 inches high at the front
InteriorWorking GFI outlets, no keyed locks on bedroom doors or inside egress doors, no junk or debris

Source: Edison Township Residential Resale Certificate Application.

sections.h2: What if work was done on the house without a permit?
sections.html:
• The form says the current owner must resolve it, even if a previous owner did the work.
  • You pull a compliance permit, have the work inspected and close the permit before the certificate is issued.
  • Before the inspection, check the Building Department for open permits and ask the Tax Assessor whether improvements such as a finished basement are on the township record.
  • The ordinance covers every change of ownership, so a sale to a cash buyer still needs the certificate before closing.

Open permits are the most common reason an Edison closing slips. Ask the Building Department for a permit history on the address as soon as you list.

sections.h2: What does Edison look like to a buyer?
sections.html:
Edison surrounds the borough of Metuchen and touches East Brunswick, Highland Park, New Brunswick, Piscataway, Sayreville, South Plainfield and Woodbridge in Middlesex County, plus Clark, Plainfield and Scotch Plains in Union County. The township sits roughly 27 miles from both Midtown Manhattan and Trenton.

  • Rail: Edison station in South Edison runs NJ Transit Northeast Corridor trains to Newark Penn, New York Penn and Trenton, and North Edison residents may be closer to Metropark or Metuchen stations.
  • Roads: Route 27, Route 440, U.S. Route 1, Interstate 287 and about five miles of the New Jersey Turnpike, with Exit 10 inside the township.
  • Jobs: Raritan Center, a 2,300 acre business park, plus the state's largest private convention center, warehouse hubs and an Amazon fulfillment center.

Census workers here spend 33.9 minutes getting to their jobs on average.

sections.h2: How does Edison's weather show up in a home inspection?
sections.html:
The township's climate is humid subtropical, and rain and melted snow add up to about 49.6 inches a year, the wettest stretch running through late summer, and snow falls several times each winter. Recorded extremes run from minus 17 degrees in 1934 to 106 degrees in 1936 and 1949.

A buyer's inspector will therefore look closely at the roof, gutters and basement walls, and the township checklist adds the water heater and stair rails. Fixing a damp basement corner or a loose guardrail before you list costs less than negotiating it after the inspection report.

Edison Township Public Schools serve pre-kindergarten through grade 12 and split the township between two high schools. Homes in the south feed Edison High School, and homes in the north feed J.P. Stevens High School. The district reported 16,268 students across 19 schools for 2021-22. Families also look at the Greater Brunswick Charter School and the Middlesex County Magnet Schools, which accept applications from eighth graders countywide.

When you list, name the attendance zone for the street you are on. The zone is part of how a listing is described.

sections.h2: How do property tax appeals and closing costs work for an Edison seller?
sections.html:
Property tax appeals go to the Middlesex County Board of Taxation, which has said it will not hold virtual hearings. The state deadline is April 1, moved to May 1 where a municipality has done a revaluation.

At closing the seller pays the state realty transfer fee. The state's own example shows $1,910 on a $325,000 deed with no exemption. Edison sellers who live in New Jersey sign GIT/REP-3 to record the deed, while nonresident sellers use GIT/REP-1 or GIT/REP-2 unless they qualify under a seller's assurance.

sections.h2: Where does the deed get recorded in Edison?
sections.html:
The Middlesex County Clerk records every deed for Edison at the County Administration Building, 75 Bayard Street, New Brunswick. The office takes walk-ins on weekdays, opening at 8:30 and closing at 4:10, with a 4:00 arrival cutoff. Paper filings need a cover sheet, and skipping it adds a $20 indexing charge. The deed must say "Prepared by," list tax block, lot and consideration, and carry a return address.

Most Edison closings go through an attorney or title company that records electronically, so this matters mainly when you sell without one.

faqs.q: How much does the Edison resale certificate cost?
faqs.a: The township form lists a $150 fee. It must be paid by certified check, credit card or money order, and the form states there are no cash payments, no personal checks and no refunds. Fines of up to $2,000 apply if you close without the certificate.

faqs.q: Do I need the smoke certificate before the Edison inspection?
faqs.a: Yes. The form says the smoke certificate is required before the resale certificate can be issued. If the Fire Prevention inspection happens first, give the inspector a copy at the resale visit or email it to the township's resale address.

faqs.q: Can I sell an Edison house with a finished basement that has no permit?
faqs.a: You can sell it, but the certificate will not issue until a permit is obtained, the work passes inspection and the permit is closed. Check with the Building Department and the Tax Assessor before you schedule the inspection.

faqs.q: Which county office records an Edison deed?
faqs.a: The Middlesex County Clerk in New Brunswick. The office is open weekdays from 8:30 a.m. and requires arrival by 4:00 p.m., and paper documents need a cover sheet.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to appeal an Edison property tax assessment?
faqs.a: April 1 of the tax year, or May 1 when the township completed a revaluation. File with the Middlesex County Board of Taxation. Properties assessed above $1,000,000 can go straight to the State Tax Court.
